How Much Is a Costco Membership in 2026? Full Guide & Deals
Wondering how much a Costco membership costs and whether it’s worth it for your family or business? Costco is one of the most popular membership warehouse clubs in the U.S., offering unbeatable deals on groceries, electronics, and household essentials. With multiple membership tiers, exclusive rewards, and the Costco Anywhere Visa Card, it can be hard to know which option is right for you. In this guide, we break down Costco membership prices, the difference between all of Costco memberships, how to sign up, and what benefits you’ll actually get — helping you make an informed decision and maximize your savings in 2026
Costco Membership 2026: Quick Navigation & Guide
How Much Is a Costco Membership? (Costco Membership Price in 2026)
Costco offers three main types of memberships, each with different prices and perks. Here’s a quick overview of the Costco membership price for 2026:
Gold Star Membership: $65 per year – Standard membership for individuals and families.
Business Membership: $65 per year – Designed for business owners and resale purposes.
Executive Membership: $130 per year – Premium membership with 2% annual rewards on purchases and extra benefits.
All memberships include access to Costco warehouses, the ability to shop online, and the option to add additional cardholders. Prices are annual and subject to state taxes, but these memberships remain one of the best value options for bulk shopping and exclusive deals in 2026.
Difference Between All of Costco Memberships
One of the most common questions shoppers ask is what is the difference between Costco memberships. Understanding the differences helps you choose the right plan based on your shopping habits, business needs, and desired rewards. Here’s a breakdown of the three main membership types in 2026:
Membership Type — Annual Cost — Who It’s For — Key Benefits
Gold Star — $65 — Individuals & families — Access to warehouses & online shopping, 2 membership cards, basic discounts
Business — $65 — Business owners & resale purposes — Resale purchases, add affiliate cardholders, warehouse & online access
Executive — $130 — Frequent shoppers & businesses seeking rewards — 2% annual reward on purchases, extra services, exclusive promotions, warehouse & online access
Key Differences at a Glance
Gold Star: Ideal for casual shoppers looking for savings and standard access.
Business: Great for small business owners and resellers who need extra cards and resale privileges.
Executive: Best for frequent shoppers who want 2% cashback and exclusive perks.
By comparing these options, you can clearly see the difference between all of Costco memberships and decide which plan fits your lifestyle and budget in 2026.
Are There Free or Discounted Costco Membership Options?
Many shoppers wonder if there are ways to save on a Costco membership. While Costco does not offer completely free memberships, there are a few ways to reduce the cost or enjoy added perks:
Executive Upgrade Discounts: Occasionally, Costco offers promotions to upgrade from Gold Star or Business to Executive at a reduced price.
Corporate or Employer Programs: Some employers provide discounted or reimbursed membership fees for employees.
Gift Memberships: Members can receive promotional gift memberships for friends or family, which can help offset costs.
Special Promotions: Certain regional warehouses may run seasonal promotions offering incentives for new members.
While a completely free membership is rare, these options allow shoppers to maximize value and potentially save on the Costco membership price in 2026.
Keep in mind that all membership types still grant access to online shopping and warehouse benefits, so even discounted memberships can deliver significant savings.
Is Costco Worth It? (Costco Membership Benefits)
Many shoppers ask, is Costco worth it? The answer depends on your shopping habits, household size, and whether you value bulk savings and exclusive perks. Here’s a breakdown of the key Costco membership benefits in 2026:
1. Significant Savings on Bulk Purchases
Costco is known for its competitive pricing on groceries, electronics, and household essentials. Buying in bulk can save money over time, making memberships especially valuable for families and small businesses.
2. Access to Executive Rewards
Executive members receive a 2% annual reward on qualifying purchases, up to $1,250 per year. This can quickly offset the higher membership fee and make frequent shopping trips more profitable.
3. Exclusive Services and Perks
Costco pharmacy discounts and health services
Optical and hearing aid centers
Travel deals and auto services
Online shopping access with home delivery
4. Costco Anywhere Visa Card
Members who have the Costco Anywhere Visa Card enjoy cashback rewards on gas, travel, and restaurant purchases, adding even more value beyond warehouse shopping.
Overall, if you regularly shop at Costco or take advantage of its online and in-store perks, a membership can quickly pay for itself, making it well worth the investment in 2026.
How Do You Pay for Purchases at Costco?
Understanding how to pay for purchases at Costco is important, especially if you plan to shop frequently or online. Costco accepts several payment methods, but there are a few specifics to know:
Debit cards – most major debit cards are accepted at warehouse locations.
Cash – you can pay with cash at any Costco warehouse.
Checks – personal checks are accepted, but they require ID verification.
Costco Cash Card (gift card) – can be used for any purchase, including groceries and gas.
Bring your membership card – you must be a member to make purchases in-store or online.
Plan your payment method – remember that most major credit cards are not accepted in-store.
Use gift cards or debit cards as backup if you don’t have a Costco Anywhere Visa® Card.
Costco Anywhere Visa® Card Benefits
The Costco Anywhere Visa® Card is the only credit card accepted in-store and offers valuable rewards, including 2% cashback on eligible purchases, cashback on gas, travel, and dining, making it the best choice for maximizing your Costco membership benefits.
How Do You Sign Up for a Costco Membership?
Signing up for a Costco membership is quick and easy in 2026. You can do it online, in-store, or take advantage of a special Groupon deal to save on your membership fee:
Sign Up via Groupon (Discounted Membership)
Start your Costco membership today with this discounted Costco membership deal on Groupon . This is a fast and affordable way to enjoy all the perks, including warehouse shopping, online access, and the Costco Anywhere Visa® Card benefits.
Choose your membership type: Gold Star, Business, or Executive.
Fill out your personal or business information.
Enter payment information to pay your annual membership fee securely online, or use the Groupon deal link for savings.
After payment, you’ll receive confirmation and a digital membership card that can be used immediately for online shopping.
Visit your nearest Costco warehouse and head to the membership counter.
Provide personal or business details and a valid photo ID.
Pay the annual membership fee using cash, debit card, or the Costco Anywhere Visa® Card.
Receive your physical membership card immediately and start shopping in-store or online.
Consider the Executive membership for 2% cashback rewards and extra benefits.
Keep your membership number handy for online shopping and renewals.
Check Groupon or employer promotions to get the best deal on your first year.
By signing up via the Groupon link above, you can get started quickly while taking advantage of exclusive 2026 savings and start enjoying the full range of Costco membership benefits immediately.
Frequently Asked Questions About Costco Membership
Do I need a membership to shop at Costco?
Yes. A Costco membership is required for both in-store and online purchases. Without a membership, you cannot make regular purchases, though some gift cards may allow limited access.
Can I share my Costco membership?
Yes. Gold Star and Executive memberships come with one free household card, and Business memberships can add additional cardholders. This allows family members or employees to shop under the same account.
What is the difference between Costco memberships?
The main differences are price and benefits. Gold Star and Business memberships cost $65/year, while Executive costs $130/year and includes 2% cashback on purchases and exclusive services. Business memberships also allow resale privileges and additional cardholders.
Are there free or discounted Costco membership options?
While Costco does not typically offer free memberships, you can save through promotions, corporate programs, or the discounted Costco membership deal on Groupon.
Is Executive membership worth it?
If you shop frequently at Costco or spend enough annually, the Executive membership can pay for itself through 2% cashback and extra benefits, making it a good option for families and businesses in 2026.
How do I pay for purchases at Costco?
Payment methods include the Costco Anywhere Visa® Card (in-store and online), debit cards, cash, personal checks, and Costco Cash Cards. The Visa card is recommended for maximizing rewards and cashback benefits.

results.title: Costco Membership: What to Know, Perks, Fees and More
results.content:

Costco is one of America’s most beloved membership warehouse chains — there are fan Facebook groups and some devout fans have even gotten married inside the store. With almost 900 locations in nine countries and nearly 137 million cardholders, Costco is also one of the largest membership warehouse chains worldwide. But how does the whole thing work? Is it a grocery store? Do they sell couches? Can I get my tires rotated there? The answer to all these questions is, “yes.”
Below, I break down everything you should know about Costco, from its annual membership fees to the store’s various offerings. I’ve been a Costco member for several years, and I’ve personally used and enjoyed many of these services.
Want more from NBC Select? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter.
Costco is a warehouse club, which means, unlike typical grocery stores, it sells goods in bulk in order to provide discounted prices. Aside from groceries, it also sells clothing, toys, electronics and more. When Costco opened its first store in the 1970s, it initially sold only to small businesses but it expanded to cater to individuals in the 1980s.
Yes, you need a membership in order to shop at a Costco. If you know someone with a membership, they can bring you with them to the store, but the primary cardholder will have to make all purchases.
It is possible to shop via Costco’s website without a membership, but non-members have access to only select deals, and online prices are often higher than in-store ones.
There are three types of Costco memberships, all of which give you access to every Costco location worldwide:
The Gold Star Membership is the cheapest option for customers who aren’t affiliated with a business. The annual membership fee is $65, and a total of two people over the age of 18 living at the same address can use the membership. This membership also allows you to shop online and in stores.
The Executive Membership costs $130 a year and comes with a total of two Household Cards. This tier offers greater savings on Costco services and select Costco Travel packages, as well as an annual 2% reward on qualified Costco purchases. With some strategic shopping, the higher fee may be worth it. For instance, if you spend $3,000 annually on qualified purchases like groceries, furniture and electronics, you’ll receive $60 back, which is roughly the cost of the tier upgrade. This membership also allows for exclusive shopping hours that Gold Star members don’t have access to.
The Business Membership also costs $65 a year, but is exclusively for business owners to buy products for business, personal and resale use. The membership has the option to add a member of your household for no extra charge or you can add additional cardholders for $65 a year. In order to qualify for the Business Membership, you have to show some type of business identification, like a business license or three types of business ID.
Every Costco member has access to benefits like discounted contact lenses, travel packages and more, with greater savings on Costco services and select travel packages available to Executive members.
Costco is perhaps best known for its bulk discounts on groceries and other household essentials, with deals ranging from a two-pack of 1 ½-liter bottles of Listerine to a 30-pack of Lorna Doone Shortbread Cookies.
Some of Costco’s best deals are on products from its popular in-house brand, Kirkland Signature: A 120-pack of Breakfast Blend K-Cup Pods, for instance, is $36.99 (discounted from its regular $44.99 price), while a 72-count of Dunkin Donuts' Original Blend K-Cup Pods is $38.99. Under the Kirkland name, Costco also sells clothing, vitamins, beauty and skin care items, pet food, pans and more.
Costco members in certain locations have access to same-day delivery via Instacart to have perishables delivered to your door. But if you’re taking home your own groceries (or anything, really), you need to bring your own bags. I personally prefer to bring large boxes since they’re easier to carry up the stairs to my condo.
Outside of groceries and home essentials, Costco is known for its comparatively low gas prices. The conglomerate sells its own Kirkland Signature Gasoline, which is designed with deposit control additives to help clean your car’s engine and keep it running smoothly, according to the company. You can find nearby locations with gas stations via Costco’s website.
Whether you need a couch, an air fryer, a TV or running shoes, Costco has a vast selection of clothing, furniture and other home essentials from popular brands like Adidas, Casper, and LG. With a Costco membership, you also get in-home delivery and installation on major appliances as well as a two-year Costco extended warranty. Costco also constantly offers additional markdowns on certain brands and products, so make sure to check its website for promotions.
Both Gold Star and Executive members have benefits through Costco Travel, but only Executive members earn 2% rewards with purchases, according to the brand. Members can book car rentals, vacation packages, cruises, hotel stays and more, but only with Costco’s travel partners — when booking a car, for instance, you can only choose from Alamo, Avis, Budget and Enterprise. And Costco’s prices aren’t always the cheapest available, so compare across booking sites before making reservations.
A Costco membership (both Gold Star and Executive) can score you discounts on new and pre-owned vehicles. The Costco Auto Program will connect members to local, pre-vetted pre-owned-vehicle dealers offering prearranged pricing for Costco members. If you already own a car, Costco also sells discounted tires (which come with a five-year Road Hazard Warranty) and batteries and offers services like rotations, balances, nitrogen tire inflation and more.
Costco provides discounted home and auto insurance to members through CONNECT, powered by American Family Insurance. Like other insurance providers, CONNECT offers additional discounts for students, safe drivers and more. Costco also sells health and vision insurance, life insurance and pet insurance, and certain plans are available for business owners as well as individuals.
Anyone can fill their prescriptions at a Costco Pharmacy, often at a competitive price compared to other pharmacies. Costco also offers the Costco Membership Prescription Program to members at no additional charge — it gives access to savings on prescriptions, though you cannot use it on top of your health insurance.
If you’re remodeling your house, redoing the floors or looking to install some new shelves, all members can book these and other home services through Costco. When you work with one of Costco’s partners, you receive a Costco Shop Card worth 10% of the cost of the service. I worked with Costco to install new shelves, for instance, and got a $350 gift card that paid for a month’s worth of groceries.
Costco has a Photo Center where members can print posters, photo books, calendars, cards and more.
Costco members have exclusive access to the Costco Anywhere Visa card, a Citi credit card with a robust rewards program. In addition to 2% cash back on eligible purchases from Costco, cardholders also get 4% cash back on eligible gas purchases up to $7,000 per year, 3% cash back on restaurants and eligible travel purchases and 1% cash back on everything else, distributed annually. Keep in mind that your Costco membership has to be active and the rewards can be used at Costco or exchanged at a warehouse for cash. There are some other credit cards with great rewards for Costco purchases to also consider, like the Chase Freedom Unlimited card and the Wells Fargo Active Cash Card.
If you are currently weighing the pros and cons of a Costco membership, then it’s likely that you’re also considering what other warehouse clubs like BJ’s and Sam’s Club have to offer. Here are two of the biggest differences to consider:
The BJ’s Inner Circle Membership is similarly priced to Costco’s Gold Star Membership at $60 a year. The BJ’s Club+ Membership is $120 a year. Unlike Costco, though, BJ’s accepts manufacturer’s coupons and you can stack them on top of the store’s built-in savings.
Sam’s Club’s Basic Membership is also similar in price at $50 a year. However, it has more limited service offerings than Costco — it doesn’t include pharmacy savings, optical savings or free shipping online, for example. The Sam’s Club Plus Membership is $110 a year.

results.title: Is a Costco Executive Membership Really Worth the Cost?
results.content:
Is a Costco Executive Membership Really Worth the Cost?
I break down the benefits so you don't have to.
Mary Jo DiLonardo has worked in journalism for 30+ years, covering topics such as lifestyle issues, health, education, and nature. Her school and pet guides for Atlanta Magazine won city and regional magazine association awards. She wrote a travel book for Random House and for sites including WebMD, CNN, & Treehugger.
Published on December 12, 2025
We were on the road recently when my husband and I decided to stop at a Costco. It was early in the morning, but we saw plenty of people streaming through the doors. When we tried, however, we were stopped. Turns out that early-morning admission is a perk for people with the executive-level membership – not ordinary members like us.
We were curious whether it was worth the extra money to get a fancy membership, so I did some digging. A standard Costco Gold Star membership costs $65 per year, compared to an Executive membership, which costs nearly double ($130 annually).
So, there are more perks with the higher-level card—but is it worth it?
Costco's Executive-Level Perks
Whichever Costco membership you have, you're able to shop online or in warehouses. It comes with an additional membership card for someone who lives in your household. With an Executive membership, there are a few additional benefits, including:
Two percent back on up to $1,250 of eligible Costco purchases each year. It comes in a check that you can spend at the warehouse store.
Early shopping hours (9-10 a.m. Sunday through Friday and 9-9:30 a.m. on Saturdays)
$10 a month credit on eligible orders of at least $150 from sameday.costco.com or Costco via Instacart
Executive-only perks on certain Costco products and services
Strictly from a financial viewpoint, you’d have to spend $3,250 a year at Costco to break even on the extra $65 in cost. (The math: two percent cashback rewards on $3,250 equals $65). That makes sense if you spend at least $270 or so each month.
If you’ve ever had the “upgrade your membership” speech from someone at Costco, the salesperson might suggest that just the purchase of one pricey laptop or television makes the extra cost worth it; the same is likely true if you book your travel through Costco. If you have major appliances or vacations on your shopping list, those could easily justify the Executive membership.
In our family, we had the Executive membership years ago but weren’t buying enough to make up the double cost of it, compared to a Gold Star membership. Now, we put all our Costco purchases on a Costco credit card—we still receive two percent back on all purchases at the club store, in addition to five percent back on gas at its pumps.
The Value of Early Shopping Hours
Rewards aside, the big question is how much that early access is worth to you. We always swear that we will "never, ever again" go to Costco on a weekend, but then somehow, we end up in the overpacked warehouse on a Saturday morning or Sunday afternoon.
If you shop at Costco frequently and really don’t have the patience to deal with all those other eager people, the extra cost of an Executive membership might be worth the peace of a quieter shopping experience.

Is a Costco membership really worth the annual fee?
Lots of people seem to think so. Costco boasted more than 145 million members in 2025 and has a U.S. renewal rate of over 90%.
While bulk groceries get the most attention, Costco’s savings can extend far beyond what ends up in your cart, from car repairs and contact lenses to travel packages and home appliances.
Here's a breakdown of what a Costco membership gets you, so you can decide if adding one more annual fee to your budget is worth it.
Costco charges annual membership fees, which start at $65. In return, members get access to discounted prices on items.
Here’s a quick glance at what each membership tier offers:
Gold Star ($65/yr)
Business ($65/yr)
Executive ($130/yr)
Who it's for
Personal use
Business owners
Personal or business
Cards included
Valid at all locations and Costco.com
Can add extra cardholders
Early store access
1 hr. early (Sun-Fri), 30 min. early (Sat)
Annual 2% reward
Up to $1,250 on qualified purchases
Let’s do some rough math to figure it out.
Costco charges a baseline price of $65 just to walk through the door. Spread out that membership cost across a full year, and you’ll need to save $5.42 per month for it to be financially “worth it.”
If you can save even $0.10 per gallon of gas, that’s $1.50 on 15 gallons. If you fill up every week, that’s $6 in savings right there.
A family of four spends between $1,000-$1,600 every month in groceries, according to USDA data. Costco wouldn’t account for all of that spending, but even if a family spends $500 a month ($6,000 a year), you’d only need to save 1% on purchases to break even. Costco advertises a 15%-20% savings compared with national brands.

Here are other ways to decide if a membership might be a good value:
✅ A Costco membership might be worth it if you:
Have kids, roommates or a larger family to shop for
Own a car and can use the Costco gas station regularly
Have storage space for bulk goods and freezer items
Book travel or rent cars occasionally
Plan to buy an appliance in the next year or two
Need affordable access to health care experts and care
❌ A Costco membership might not be worth it if you:
Have limited freezer and/or storage space
Don’t have easy access to a Costco location
Already have a membership to another warehouse store like Sam’s Club or BJ’s
I have a Gold membership, and there are things I love — the premade food is easy to grab for busy nights, and I feel like I’m getting good quality items for my money. I also trust the Kirkland store brand and appreciate Costco's workplace policies.
Costco's return policy is unmatched. I recently returned an air mattress that was a couple of years old because it got a hole — no questions asked. And getting to try the samples while I shop is always a plus.
But, I feel like the store opens too late (with young children, I’ve already lived three lives by 10 a.m.), and the line to checkout is always long. If Costco added Scan and Go like Sam’s Club, I’d never shop at another warehouse.
Costco membership perks beyond the warehouse
The food court: Costco is known for its $1.50 hot dog and soda combo, but its newest menu item — chicken tenders with dipping sauce for $6.99 — is making headlines and getting mentions on social media. The store's other popular items include a slice of pepperoni or cheese pizza ($1.99), a chicken bake ($3.99) and the double chocolate chunk cookie ($2.49). Get your kids a slice of pizza before you shop to keep them busy, like I do.
Travel deals: Members can visit Costco’s travel website to book vacation packages, hotels, cruises and rental cars. There are even theme park deals for all the Disney lovers out there.
Pharmacy: Members can get discounts on their prescriptions, schedule immunizations and pick up pet medications at lower prices. You might be trading some convenience (no drive-thru window here), but there’s a mail order option.
Shutterfly: Members save 51% on every Shutterfly order and get free economy shipping if they spend more than $30. The discount is added right to your cart (no coupon code needed). Just be sure to add your membership to your Shutterfly account to take advantage of the deal.
Sesame: Members can schedule virtual urgent care visits for $34, pay $65 for virtual therapy and more — including subscriptions for mental health, women’s health, weight loss and prescription skincare.
Home appliances: There are some benefits to buying appliances from Costco. Delivery and installation are included in the price, and Costco will haul away your old model. There’s a two-year warranty included and you can earn up to 4% in rewards.
Costco Auto Program: You might already know you can get car repairs done at Costco, and even new tires. But Costco sells cars, too. They have new and used vehicles and better deals for Executive members. Plug in your ZIP code to get a list of participating Costco dealers and local incentives.
If you’re thinking about how to leverage your Costco trip for points or credit card rewards, you might be able to earn more money back with the Costco Anywhere Visa® Card by Citi. Compare that credit card with other cash-back cards you may already carry.
I’ve been a Costco member since the year 2000. Over the years Costco has helped me save on car rentals; eyeglasses and contacts; tires; Pokémon cards; 800-thread-count sheets; diapers for my babies; two Dyson vacuums; countless photo calendars and Christmas cards; sleds; houseplants; appliances and electronics; giant slabs of wild king salmon; big ol’ jugs of Canadian maple syrup; and hunks of Gruyere. I use the home delivery service more often than I shop in-person, because, as any longtime fan knows, you don’t decide what you’re going home with from Costco: Costco decides for you!

Frequently Asked Questions
How to pay at Costco?How to pay at Costco?
Visa credit cards are the only credit card type accepted at brick-and-mortar Costco stores in the U.S. Costco also accepts debit/ATM cards, cash, checks and traveler's checks, EBT cards and mobile payment methods such as Apple Pay and Google Pay.
Costco.com accepts Mastercard in addition to Visa credit cards.
Costco allows members to bring up to two guests to shop at a warehouse, but only members can make purchases.
How do you sign up for a Costco membership?How do you sign up for a Costco membership?
To sign up, visit the membership desk at any location. You can also sign up online or by calling 1-800-774-2678.
Costco has an option to cancel your membership and receive a refund if you're dissatisfied.
Can I get a freebie membership?Can I get a freebie membership?
No. The samples are free, but Costco doesn’t provide free memberships. There are new-member promotions, such as digital shop cards, during promotional periods.
Certain groups might also qualify for discounts. Teachers, college students, medical professionals, military personnel, government employees and first responders may be eligible to receive a digital Costco gift card when they sign up.

Costco Just Added New Membership Perks for 2026—But Are They Actually Worth It?
By Ariana Losch | January 15, 2026 |
Copy this link to share with your friends!
https://sporked.com/article/costco-membership-changes-2026-news/
About two years ago (that’s 2024, for those of us who can no longer keep track of time in this freaky twilight zone we call modern life), Costco increased its annual membership fees by $5-$10. Executive Memberships went up from $120 to $130. Business Memberships increased from $60 to $65. Those rates have stayed the same since—and now, moving into 2026, Costco is supposedly adding perks intended to make that fee increase worth it. Let’s talk about them. I have thoughts, and I’d like to hear yours, too.
Changes coming to ALL Costco members this year
Costco is making digital and tech-based changes to its shopping experience. “What the hell does that mean, Ariana? Can you be any more vague?” Basically, some stores are introducing “faster” checkout systems and adding more self-checkout stands. They’re making changes to the Costco app as well, including a “password-less sign-in” that will hopefully make it easier (especially for the more tech-challenged demographic of Costco buyers) to shop online and in stores.
We reported on this last week, but Costco is also changing its food court policy to require members to scan their membership IDs to purchase food court beverages and food. That means freeloaders like myself can’t just coast in with their friend or family’s Costco membership and order a $1.50 hot dog on their own dime. Plenty of Costco stores already have this policy in place, so that might not seem like a change to many of you. But by doing this, Costco is aiming to free up space in the food courts and encourage more people to sign up for memberships.
(Also, I polled people for their thoughts on this change at the bottom of my article. Most of you are really in favor of making Costco food courts only accessible to members! I definitely disagree and will happily fight each and every one of you in the parking lot. Meet me out back. And if you’re stopping at Costco first, can you bring me a soda? I’ll venmo you the 85 cents.)
Perks coming to Executive Members only
Along with the other financial perks they already have (2% cash back on purchases, capped at $1,250), Executive Members are getting a $10 monthly credit to use on purchases over $150. Not bad, not bad. They also have the ability to cancel and refund their membership at any time, theoretically no strings attached.
It’s also worth noting that last June, Costco changed their store hours to open an hour earlier for Executive Members. They can now start shopping at 9 a.m., seven days a week. For early birds, that change alone can feel priceless.
What do you think about all of this, Ariana? I would simply love to hear your thoughts and opinions.
No, you wouldn’t, so I’ll be brief: I think the price hike that happened two years ago was not, on the whole, that bad. But I think justifying it now by merely addressing a well-known problem with Costco—the fact that it’s busy as hell, with lines and crowds that can feel nightmarish—and calling it a membership “perk” makes me roll my eyes a little. That’s okay, though. I will always roll my eyes at companies that increase prices and pretend it has nothing to do with general inflation. And honestly, Executive Members are getting some good perks on the whole that might be worth that $130 price point. Man, that wasn’t as brief as I thought it would be. More importantly: What do YOU think about the changes coming to Costco? Tell me in the comments? Please?
